intro.title: Explore Dubovyy Hay
intro.description: Dubovyy Hay (Дубовий Гай) is located in Zaporizhzhia, Zaporizhzhia Oblast, Ukraine. It is a beautiful urban park that serves as an ideal place for locals and tourists to relax and unwind. With its rich greenery and pleasant environment, the park is one of the important green spaces in Zaporizhzhia, providing not only leisure space for citizens but also an excellent vantage point to experience the natural charm of Zaporizhzhia.

Historical Ruins & Water Features: The park preserves grand abandoned buildings and tranquil ponds, adding a unique retro atmosphere to this urban oasis.

intro.summary: Dubovyy Hay, known officially as «Дубовий Гай», is Zaporizhzhia’s main city park (Zaporizhzhia Oblast, Ukraine). Tree-lined paths, lakes with bridges, concert areas and a small amusement park make it a favourite year-round spot for locals and visitors. This guide helps you plan your visit to Dubovyy Hay in Zaporizhzhia.

knowledge.title: Discover the Charm of Dubovyy Hay

sections.title: Historical Significance
sections.content: Dubovyy Hay is an important park in Zaporizhzhia, providing recreational space for local residents and tourists. The park has witnessed the development and changes of Zaporizhzhia city.

sections.title: Natural Landscape
sections.content: The park is planted with various plants, with shaded trees forming a green canopy, making it a rare natural oasis in the city. Visitors can enjoy peaceful moments here and feel the breath of nature.

sections.title: Recreation Experience
sections.content: Dubovyy Hay is the best place to experience Zaporizhzhia's urban natural atmosphere. You can sit on a bench in the park to rest, stroll along the tree-lined paths, or simply enjoy a moment of tranquility.

officialManagement.title: About Dubovyy Hay
officialManagement.text: Dubovyy Hay is an important park in Zaporizhzhia, managed and maintained by the Zaporizhzhia City Government.

story.title: History & Local Legends
story.subtitle: Behind every old oak lies a century of the city’s memory
story.introText: “Dubovyi Hai” literally means “oak grove” in Ukrainian. As early as the 18th century, the left bank of the Dnipro here was covered with vast oak woods stretching toward the wide floodplain known as the Velykyi Luh (Great Meadow) — lands closely tied to the history of the Zaporozhian Cossacks. In Ukrainian culture the oak stands for strength and watchfulness, so long before the park existed, this land was already part of Zaporizhzhia’s living memory.
story.timelineTitle: Timeline: from a riverside oak wood to the city’s green heart

timeline.title: Ancient oaks by the river
timeline.text: This area was once an old oak woodland on the floodplain of the Dnipro. In Cossack times the oaks supplied timber and fuel, and served as natural landmarks where people rested and gathered.

timeline.title: A place for local festivities
timeline.text: From the 19th century, the grassy clearings under the oaks became a favourite spot for picnics and celebrations. May outings and family gatherings made the old trees silent witnesses of many generations.

timeline.title: The beginnings of the green zone
timeline.text: In 1956 the area began to be maintained as an urban green space, preparing the ground for the park that would follow.

timeline.title: The Central Park of Culture and Rest opens
timeline.text: The park officially opened on 1 May 1959 with a total area of more than 57 hectares — roughly the size of 80 football pitches. Over the following decades, tree-lined alleys, fountains and gazebos in the style of the era, an open-air cinema and a main stage were built, making the park a shared leisure memory of generations of Zaporizhzhia residents.

timeline.title: A star of the silver screen
timeline.text: In the 1950s, the classic Soviet film “Spring on Zarechnaya Street” (Vesna na Zarechnoy ulitse) was shot here. After the film was released, the name of this oak grove travelled across the whole country on the screen.

timeline.title: A walkable green oasis
timeline.text: Today the park is managed as a pedestrian-friendly space: vehicle access is restricted, accessibility and children’s facilities keep improving, and festivals, sports events, exhibitions and family activities are held all year round. It is both the “green lungs” of Zaporizhzhia and a living room for its people in every season.

story.legendsTitle: Legends passed from mouth to mouth
story.legendsNote: The stories below belong to Zaporizhzhia’s local folklore and oral tradition. Handed down over many years, they are not necessarily supported by formal historical records, so we suggest enjoying them as cultural background for your visit.

legends.title: Oaks planted by the Cossacks
legends.text: Tradition says the oaks were planted by the Zaporozhian Cossacks themselves, to remember the Zaporozhian Sich that was destroyed in the turmoil of war. People say the Cossacks planted the trees in tears, and that is why the oaks took root so deeply and never stopped growing — guarding the land’s memory of freedom.

legends.title: The “Makhno Oak”
legends.text: At the edge of the park there once stood a famous old oak with iron nails, bolts and spikes embedded in its trunk. Folklore links the tree to the military figure Nestor Makhno: his followers supposedly used the iron pieces to climb into the crown and set an ambush. The old tree died and was removed in the 1970s, yet the story still lives on locally.

legends.title: The watch-post in the treetops
legends.text: Another tale from before the revolution says that workers held their May outings (mayivka) here and posted lookouts in the oaks to raise the alarm if gendarmes or raids appeared. True or not, these stories add a touch of legend to the old oaks.

names.title: Official name and local nicknames
names.paragraph: Locals often simply call the park “Dubovka”. In Russian it is also known as «Дубовый Гай» or «Дубовая роща», while English guidebooks and maps mostly use Dubovyy Hay or Dubovka.

nature.title: Nature & Wildlife
nature.subtitle: A 57-hectare green classroom with the city’s most vivid seasons
nature.intro: The park covers more than 57 hectares, about 5 of which belong to the nature reserve fund. Its old oaks are said to reach about 300 years of age, making the park one of the most ecologically valuable green spaces in Zaporizhzhia and a natural classroom for urban nature.

highlights.title: Old oaks with stories
highlights.text: The oaks gave the grove its name. Alongside ancient trees of 100–200 years or more, the park mixes many species of trees, shrubs and wildflowers, so every season — from fresh spring green to golden autumn leaves — brings its own scenery.

highlights.title: Artificial lakes and two bridges
highlights.text: The park has an artificial lake crossed by two footbridges. In the warm months you can hire a pedal boat and glide slowly across the water, with weeping willows and mirror reflections making a classic photo scene.

highlights.title: A small river along the edge
highlights.text: The Mokra Moskovka river winds along one side of the park. Its wetland banks create a unique riverside habitat and keep a wild touch in the very heart of the city.

highlights.title: A “birdwatching point” in the city
highlights.text: Tall crowns and calm water attract many birds. Ducks and geese paddle by the ponds, and the treetops ring with birdsong — a lovely place to meet urban wildlife up close.

nature.note: Please enjoy nature responsibly: do not disturb the waterbirds or throw litter into the lake; if you feed the birds, choose suitable food or follow the park’s guidance so this urban oasis stays safe for everyone.

amenities.title: Practical Facilities
amenities.subtitle: Restrooms, parking, dining, stays, shops, fuel & charging — check before you go
amenities.intro: Dubovyi Hai is an open, free-to-enter park centred on walking trails and greenery. Below we summarise, by category, the facilities you may need during your visit to help you plan with ease.

toilet.title: Public Restrooms
toilet.text: Public restrooms are available near the main entrances, the amusement area and the event zones. They can get busy on holidays and weekends, so the facilities by the entrances are a good first choice — please also mind their opening hours.

parking.title: Parking
parking.text: Limited public parking is available on the streets near the park and along the riverside; some spaces are paid. Spaces fill up quickly on weekends and holidays, so arrive early or consider public transport or a taxi.

dining.title: Dining
dining.text: Inside the park you will find cafés and food kiosks offering snacks, hot and cold drinks and light meals. The city centre around the park has restaurants serving traditional Ukrainian cuisine, plus various other cuisines and street food. Always check the current opening status on site.

hotel.title: Accommodation
hotel.text: As an open public space, the park itself offers no overnight stays. For an overnight trip, choose among hotels, guesthouses and short-term apartments in Zaporizhzhia city centre and nearby areas; reaching the park from there by taxi or public transport is easy.

shopping.title: Supermarkets & Convenience Stores
shopping.text: Supermarkets, convenience stores and pharmacies can be found near the park and along the city’s main streets, so you can easily buy drinking water, snacks or essentials. Banks and ATMs are available in the city centre if you need cash or currency exchange.

fuel.title: Fuel & EV Charging
fuel.text: Self-drive visitors can find petrol stations along the city’s main roads, and public charging points for electric cars are gradually increasing. Before you leave, plan a route with a convenient station using a map app and confirm it is currently open.

faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.subtitle: Answers to the questions visitors most often ask about Dubovyy Hay.

items.q: Do I need a ticket to enter Dubovyy Hay park?
items.a: No. Dubovyy Hay is an open city park: entry is free and the park is open 24 hours. Only rides and on-site services (e.g. paid parking) are charged separately.

items.q: What rides and facilities are in the park?
items.a: The park has an amusement area with a well-known Ferris wheel, as well as lakes with bridges, children’s and sports playgrounds. Always check the current list and opening hours of the rides before your visit.

items.q: How do I get to Dubovyy Hay park?
items.a: The park lies on the Dnipro riverfront at Hliserna Street, 1 (Plus Code: R56C+75 Zaporizhzhia). Detailed options — by public transport, car or on foot — are gathered in the Transport section of this page.

items.q: Is there parking near the park?
items.a: On-street parking in Zaporizhzhia is generally limited. There are public spots, partly paid, near the park and along the embankment; they fill up on weekends and holidays, so public transport or a taxi is often easier.

items.q: Is the park suitable for children?
items.a: Yes, it is a popular family destination with playgrounds, rides, open lawns and cafés. Check current pet rules and facility opening hours on site.

items.q: When is the best time to visit Dubovyy Hay?
items.a: The park is lovely year-round: green and lively by the lakes in spring and summer, open for relaxed walks in winter. Expect crowds during holiday events.
